question_text: Explain on the basis of valence bond theory that [Ni(CN)4]2- ion with square planar structure is diamagnetic and the [NiCl]2- ion with tetrahedral geometry is paramagnetic.
answer_text: Ni is in the +2 oxidation state i.e., in d8 configuration. There are 4 CN- ions. Thus, it can either have a tetrahedral geometry or square planar geometry. Since CN- ion is a strong field ligand, it causes the pairing of unpaired 3d electrons. It now undergoes dsp2 hybridization. Since all electrons are paired, it is diamagnetic. In case of [NiCl]2-, Cl- ion is a weak field ligand. Therefore, it does not lead to the pairing of unpaired 3d electrons. Therefore, it undergoes sp3 hybridization. Since there are 2 unpaired electrons in this case, it is paramagnetic in nature.

Identify the weak field nature of Cl- in [NiCl]2- and its effect on electron pairing.
Explain the hybridization of [NiCl]2- and conclude it is paramagnetic.

final_answer: Thus, [Ni(CN)4]2- is diamagnetic due to paired electrons, while [NiCl]2- is paramagnetic due to unpaired electrons.

question_text: [NiCl]2- is paramagnetic while [Ni(CO)] is diamagnetic though both are tetrahedral. Why?
answer_text: Though both [NiCl]2- and [Ni(CO)] are tetrahedral, their magnetic characters are different. This is due to a difference in the nature of ligands. Cl- is a weak field ligand and it does not cause the pairing of unpaired 3d electrons. Hence, [NiCl]2- is paramagnetic. In Ni(CO), Ni is in the zero oxidation state i.e., it has a configuration of 3d8 4s2. But CO is a strong field ligand. Therefore, it causes the pairing of unpaired 3d electrons. Also, it causes the 4s electrons to shift to the 3d orbital, thereby giving rise to sp3 hybridization. Since no unpaired electrons are present in this case, [Ni(CO)] is diamagnetic.

Explain the weak field nature of Cl- leading to unpaired electrons.
Identify the ligand strength of CO and its effect on electron pairing in [Ni(CO)].
Explain the strong field nature of CO leading to paired electrons.

final_answer: Thus, [NiCl]2- is paramagnetic due to unpaired electrons, while [Ni(CO)] is diamagnetic due to paired electrons.

subject: chemistry
question_text: Explain with two examples each of the following: coordination entity, ligand, coordination number, coordination polyhedron, homoleptic and heteroleptic.

question_image.description: Diagram illustrating coordination polyhedrons and examples of coordination entities.

answer_text: Coordination entity: A coordination entity is an electrically charged radical or species carrying a positive or negative charge. Examples include cationic complex [Cu(NH3)6]2+, anionic complex [Fe(CN)6]3-, and neutral complex [CoCl3(NH3)3]. Ligands are neutral molecules or negatively charged ions that surround the metal atom. Examples include H2O, Cl-, and OH-. Coordination number is the total number of ligands attached to the central metal atom. For example, in K[PtCl6], the coordination number of Pt is 6, and in [Ni(NH3)4]Cl2, the coordination number of Ni is 4. Coordination polyhedron refers to the spatial arrangement of ligands around the central metal ion. Examples include octahedral and tetrahedral arrangements. Homoleptic complexes have only one type of ligand, while heteroleptic complexes have more than one type of ligand.
final_answer: Thus, these definitions and examples illustrate the concepts of coordination entities, ligands, coordination numbers, coordination polyhedra, and the distinction between homoleptic and heteroleptic complexes.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of multiple concepts and definitions in coordination chemistry.

(i) a green precipitate with aqueous potassium fluoride, and

answer_text: Aqueous CuSO4 exists as [Cu(H2O)6]SO4. It is blue in colour due to the presence of [Cu(H2O)6]2+ ions. When KF is added, the weak field ligand water is replaced by F- ions, resulting in a green precipitate. Similarly, KCl replaces water with Cl- ions, forming a bright green solution.

question_text: What is spectrochemical series? Explain the difference between a weak field ligand and a strong field ligand.
answer_text: A spectrochemical series is the arrangement of common ligands in the increasing order of their crystal-field splitting energy (CFSE) values. The ligands present on the R.H.S of the series are strong field ligands while that on the L.H.S are weak field ligands. Also, strong field ligands cause higher splitting in the d orbitals than weak field ligands.
final_answer: Thus, the spectrochemical series distinguishes between weak and strong field ligands based on their ability to split d-orbitals.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of ligand properties and their effects on d-orbital splitting.

subject: chemistry
question_text: What is crystal field splitting energy? How does the magnitude of Δ decide the actual configuration of d-orbitals in a coordination entity?
answer_text: The degenerate d-orbitals (in a spherical field environment) split into two levels i.e., e and t in the presence of ligands. The splitting of the degenerate levels due to the presence of ligands is called the crystal-field splitting while the energy difference between the two levels (e and t) is called the crystal-field splitting energy. It is denoted by Δ. After the orbitals have split, the filling of the electrons takes place. If the Δ value of a ligand is less than the pairing energy (P), then the electrons enter the e orbital. On the other hand, if the Δ value of a ligand is more than the pairing energy (P), then the electrons enter the t orbital.
final_answer: Therefore, the magnitude of Δ determines whether electrons will pair up or occupy higher energy orbitals.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of electronic configurations and energy levels in coordination complexes.

question_text: [Cr(NH3)6]3+ is paramagnetic while [Ni(CN)6]2- is diamagnetic. Explain why?
answer_text: Cr is in the +3 oxidation state i.e., d3 configuration. NH3 is a weak field ligand that does not cause the pairing of the electrons in the 3d orbital. Therefore, it undergoes d2sp3 hybridization and the electrons in the 3d orbitals remain unpaired, making it paramagnetic. In [Ni(CN)6]2-, Ni exists in the +2 oxidation state i.e., d8 configuration. CN- is a strong field ligand that causes the pairing of the 3d orbital electrons. As there are no unpaired electrons, it is diamagnetic.
final_answer: Thus, the difference in the ligand strength leads to different magnetic properties in these complexes.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of ligand effects on electron pairing and magnetic properties.

question_text: A solution of [Ni(H2O)6]2+ is green but a solution of [Ni(CN)6]2- is colourless. Explain.
answer_text: [Ni(H2O)6]2+ is a weak field ligand, leading to unpaired electrons in Ni2+. This allows for d-d transitions, resulting in color. In contrast, [Ni(CN)6]2- has all paired electrons due to CN- being a strong field ligand, preventing d-d transitions and making it colorless.
final_answer: Therefore, the color difference arises from the presence or absence of unpaired electrons.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of ligand effects on color and electron transitions.

subject: chemistry
question_text: Discuss the nature of bonding in metal carbonyls.
answer_text: The metal-carbon bonds in metal carbonyls have both σ and π characters. A σ bond is formed when the carbonyl carbon donates a lone pair of electrons to the vacant orbital of the metal. A π bond is formed by the donation of a pair of electrons from the filled metal d orbital into the vacant anti-bonding π* orbital (also known as back bonding of the carbonyl group). The σ bond strengthens the π bond and vice-versa. Thus, a synergic effect is created due to this metal-ligand bonding. This synergic effect strengthens the bond between CO and the metal.
final_answer: Thus, a synergic effect is created due to this metal-ligand bonding.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of metal-ligand bonding concepts.

subject: chemistry
question_text: What is meant by stability of a coordination compound in solution? State the factors which govern stability of complexes.
answer_text: The stability of a complex in a solution refers to the degree of association between the two species involved in a state of equilibrium. Stability can be expressed quantitatively in terms of stability constant or formation constant. For this reaction, the greater the value of the stability constant, the greater is the proportion of ML in the solution. Stability can be of two types: (a) Thermodynamic stability: The extent to which the complex will be formed or will be transformed into another species at the point of equilibrium is determined by thermodynamic stability. (b) Kinetic stability: This helps in determining the speed with which the transformation will occur to attain the state of equilibrium. Factors that affect the stability of a complex are: (a) Charge on the central metal ion: The greater the charge on the central metal ion, the greater is the stability of the complex. (b) Basic nature of the ligand: A more basic ligand will form a more stable complex. (c) Presence of chelate rings: Chelation increases the stability of complexes.
final_answer: Thus, the stability of coordination compounds in solution is influenced by thermodynamic and kinetic factors, as well as the nature of the metal ion and ligands involved.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of concepts and multiple factors affecting stability.

subject: chemistry
question_text: What is meant by the chelate effect? Give an example.
answer_text: When a ligand attaches to the metal ion in a manner that forms a ring, then the metal-ligand association is found to be more stable. In other words, we can say that complexes containing chelate rings are more stable than complexes without rings. This is known as the chelate effect.
final_answer: Therefore, the chelate effect describes the increased stability of complexes formed with ligands that create ring structures.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves basic understanding of ligand behavior and stability concepts.

(i) biological system
(ii) medicinal chemistry
(iii) analytical chemistry
(iv) extraction/metallurgy of metals

question_image.description: Image related to coordination compounds, possibly showing examples or structures.

parts.part_text: Role of coordination compounds in biological systems: We know that photosynthesis is made possible by the presence of the chlorophyll pigment. This pigment is a coordination compound of magnesium. In the human biological system, several coordination compounds play important roles. For example, the oxygen-carrier of blood, i.e., haemoglobin, is a coordination compound of iron.
parts.answer_text: Chlorophyll and haemoglobin are examples of coordination compounds in biological systems.
parts.final_answer: Thus, coordination compounds are crucial in biological systems.

parts.part_text: Role of coordination compounds in medicinal chemistry: Certain coordination compounds of platinum (for example, cis-platin) are used for inhibiting the growth of tumours.
parts.answer_text: Cis-platin is a coordination compound used in cancer treatment.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, coordination compounds play a significant role in medicinal chemistry.

parts.part_text: Role of coordination compounds in analytical chemistry: During salt analysis, a number of basic radicals are detected with the help of the colour changes they exhibit with different reagents. These colour changes are a result of the coordination compounds or complexes that the basic radicals form with different ligands.
parts.answer_text: Coordination compounds are used to detect basic radicals through color changes.
parts.final_answer: Thus, they are essential in analytical chemistry.

parts.part_text: Role of coordination compounds in extraction or metallurgy of metals: The process of extraction of some of the metals from their ores involves the formation of complexes. For example, in aqueous solution, gold combines with cyanide ions to form [Au(CN)]. From this solution, gold is later extracted by the addition of zinc metal.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, coordination compounds are vital in metallurgy.
